Fit or apply a linear model predicting RM 6 7DADM from RM 8.5 7DADM

Source: R/lm_rm6_7dadm.R
lm_rm6_7dadm.Rd

Trains a simple linear regression of seven-day average daily maximum temperature (7DADM) at RM 6 on observed 7DADM at RM 8.5 using the package's built-in historical data. If newdata is supplied, the function returns a tibble of RM 6 predictions; otherwise it returns the fitted lm object for further inspection or prediction elsewhere.

Usage

lm_rm6_7dadm(newdata = NULL, months = 5:9)

Arguments

newdata

A data frame or tibble with a column named rm85_7dadm (numeric, degrees C). A date column, if present, is carried through to the output unchanged. If NULL (default), the fitted lm object is returned instead of predictions.

months

Integer vector of calendar months to include in model training. Defaults to May–September (5:9).

Value

If newdata is NULL: a fitted lm object with formula rm6_7dadm ~ rm85_7dadm, trained on historical data from the specified months.

If newdata is supplied: a tibble containing all columns from newdata plus rm6_7dadm_pred (predicted RM 6 7DADM in degrees C).

Examples

# Inspect the fitted model
m <- lm_rm6_7dadm()
summary(m)
#> 
#> Call:
#> lm(formula = rm6_7dadm ~ rm85_7dadm, data = train)
#> 
#> Residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -4.4177 -0.1599  0.0089  0.1694  1.1019 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
#> (Intercept) -0.196817   0.041598  -4.731  2.4e-06 ***
#> rm85_7dadm   1.016127   0.002315 438.926  < 2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Residual standard error: 0.3364 on 1846 degrees of freedom
#> Multiple R-squared:  0.9905,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.9905 
#> F-statistic: 1.927e+05 on 1 and 1846 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
#> 

# Predict from new RM 8.5 values
library(tibble)
new <- tibble(date = Sys.Date() + 0:6, rm85_7dadm = c(15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21))
lm_rm6_7dadm(newdata = new)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 3
#>   date       rm85_7dadm rm6_7dadm_pred
#>   <date>          <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 2026-09-16         15           15.0
#> 2 2026-09-17         16           16.1
#> 3 2026-09-18         17           17.1
#> 4 2026-09-19         18           18.1
#> 5 2026-09-20         19           19.1
#> 6 2026-09-21         20           20.1
#> 7 2026-09-22         21           21.1
